rewritten_query:
select
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    count(*) cnt1,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    count(*) cnt2,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    count(*) cnt3,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    count(*) cnt4,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    count(*) cnt5,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count,
    count(*) cnt6
from customer c
join customer_address ca
    on c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
join customer_demographics cd
    on cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
where ca.ca_county in ('Audubon County','Dade County','Dewey County','Hardeman County','Talbot County')
  and c.c_birth_month in (4, 5)
  and cd.cd_marital_status in ('M', 'U')
  and cd.cd_education_status in ('Primary', 'College', '4 yr Degree')
  and cd.cd_gender = 'M'
  and c.c_customer_sk in (
        select ss.ss_customer_sk
        from store_sales ss
        join date_dim d on ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        join item i on ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
        where d.d_year = 2001
          and d.d_moy between 1 and 4
          and i.i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
          and i.i_manager_id between 91 and 100
          and ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price between 0.17 and 0.27
  )
  and c.c_customer_sk in (
        select ws.ws_bill_customer_sk
        from web_sales ws
        join date_dim d on ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        join item i on ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
        where d.d_year = 2001
          and d.d_moy between 1 and 4
          and i.i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
          and i.i_manager_id between 91 and 100
          and ws.ws_sales_price / ws.ws_list_price between 0.17 and 0.27
        union
        select cs.cs_ship_customer_sk
        from catalog_sales cs
        join date_dim d on cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        join item i on cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
        where d.d_year = 2001
          and d.d_moy between 1 and 4
          and i.i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
          and i.i_manager_id between 91 and 100
          and cs.cs_sales_price / cs.cs_list_price between 0.17 and 0.27
  )
group by
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count
order by
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Converted correlated EXISTS subqueries (especially the OR'd web/catalog EXISTS that caused per-customer SubPlan evaluation) into uncorrelated IN subqueries, which can be hashed once and used as semi-joins. The web/catalog OR was merged into one IN subquery with UNION, producing a single hashed membership set.
Removed duplicate literal 'U' in cd_marital_status IN ('M','U','U') → IN ('M','U'). Simplified d_moy between 1 and 1+3 → between 1 and 4, and 17*0.01 / 27*0.01 → 0.17 / 0.27.
Replaced comma-style joins with explicit JOIN syntax for readability and better join-order optimization by the planner.

Given table sizes (store_sales ~28.8M, catalog_sales ~14.4M, web_sales ~7.2M, customer 500K), the uncorrelated IN subqueries allow hashed semi-joins instead of repeated correlated execution per candidate customer, dramatically reducing the nested-loop cost.
